audience: Accountants who reconcile bank statements and want to speed it up with reconciliation models.
goal: Understand the **three kinds of reconciliation model**, build a **one-click button** for recurring **bank charges**, use it to reconcile a bank charge line, and see how an **invoice-matching rule** helps you match a customer receipt to its invoice.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app, with **Configuration** and the **Dashboard**.
The bank journal you reconcile (here **Commercial Bank**) has unmatched bank lines.
You know the expense account for bank charges (here **72030110 BANK CHARGES**).
outcome: You have a **button model** for bank charges on the Commercial Bank journal.
A bank charge line was reconciled with **one click** on that button, then **Validate**.
A customer receipt was matched to its invoice and validated, and the invoice was paid down.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases.

The automated run **creates its own data**: a model named **[TEST] Bank Charges - Commercial Bank** with a random code, a bank charge line of −25.00 and a customer receipt line (the amount is the open balance of a real invoice, up to 2,800.00). The model is **deleted at the end of the run**; the reconciled lines and the invoice payment remain.

The test database already has four models: *Invoices/Bills Perfect Match*, *Invoices/Bills Partial Match if Underpaid*, *Line with Bank Fees* and *Bank Charges - Commercial Bank*. The screenshots of the reconciliation screen therefore show **two** bank-charge buttons: the existing one and the [TEST] one built in this guide.
The Partner filter in **Match Existing Entries** can hide the invoice's own receivable line. If you cannot see the invoice, remove the Partner filter and search by invoice number.
Always read the entry before you press **Validate**, and press it only once. Odoo applies the reconciliation a moment after the click.

phases.title: Look at the existing models
phases.summary: Open the list and read the invoice-matching rule.
phases.checkpoint: You know the three model types and how an invoice-matching rule is set up.

phases.title: Build the bank-charges button
phases.summary: Create a model that books a bank charge in one click.
phases.checkpoint: The **button model** is saved and appears on the Commercial Bank journal.

phases.title: Use the button on a bank charge
phases.summary: Open the reconciliation screen, press the button and validate.
phases.checkpoint: The bank charge line is reconciled and one line fewer is waiting.

phases.title: Match a receipt to its invoice
phases.summary: Use the invoice rule and Match Existing Entries.
phases.checkpoint: The receipt is validated against the invoice, which is paid down.

glossary.meaning: A saved rule or button that tells Odoo how to match or book a bank line, so you do not repeat the same work.
Adds a button to the reconciliation screen. One click builds a ready-made counterpart entry, for recurring costs such as bank charges.
Suggests a counterpart entry when a bank line fits its conditions, for example a line that includes a fee.
Looks for an open invoice or bill that fits the bank line and proposes it as the counterpart.
The rule reconciles the line by itself, so it never reaches the Reconcile screen.
A temporary account that holds a bank line until you say what it is.
The other side of a bank line: the account, invoice or bill it is booked against.
What is left over when a bank line does not exactly match what you selected.

1.title: Open the Configuration menu
1.do: In the top menu bar, click **Configuration**.
actions: If **Configuration** is hidden, click the **+** at the end of the bar.
1.see: A drop-down with the Accounting set-up entries.
1.tip: Narrow windows hide the last menu entries behind a **+**.

2.title: Open Reconciliation Models
2.where: Accounting app > Configuration > Banks > Reconciliation Models
2.why: This is where every reconciliation rule and button is defined.

3.title: Read the three types of model
actions: Look at the **Type** column (outlined in red).
Read the type of each model.
points: **Button to generate counterpart entry**: a button you press yourself.
**Rule to suggest counterpart entry**: a rule that suggests a counterpart.
**Rule to match invoices/bills**: a rule that matches invoices and bills automatically.
3.see: Each model has one of the three types.
3.why: The type decides how the model behaves.

4.title: Open the invoice matching rule
actions: Find **Invoices/Bills Perfect Match** in the list.
4.why: It shows how an automatic matching rule is set up.

5.title: Read the model type
5.do: Look at the **Type**: **Rule to match invoices/bills**.
actions: Find **Type** at the top of the form.
5.why: This type looks for an open invoice or bill that fits the bank line and proposes it as the counterpart. Nothing to click.

6.title: Read Auto-validate
actions: Find **Auto-validate** at the top right of the form.
6.see: **Auto-validate** is ticked in the test data.
6.why: When it is ticked, the rule reconciles the bank line by itself, so you never see it in the Reconcile screen. Leave it off if you want to review each match first.

7.title: Read the matching conditions
7.do: Look at the **Bank Transactions Conditions** tab.
actions: Look at the conditions in the tab.
Read the **Label** condition, **Payment Tolerance** and **Same Currency**.
7.see: The label **contains SO**, the **payment tolerance** is 0.00%, and **Same Currency** is ticked.
7.why: Conditions decide when the rule fires: the bank line label must contain the text, the amount must be within the payment tolerance, and the currency must match.

8.title: Go back to the model list
actions: Click **Reconciliation Models** at the top left.
8.why: Now you will create your own model.

9.title: Create a new model
actions: Click the **New** button at the top left.
9.why: You will build a one-click button for the monthly bank charges the bank deducts from the Commercial Bank account.

10.title: Name the model
10.see: The name appears at the top of the form.
10.why: This name is what appears on the button in the Reconcile screen.
10.tip: Make the name say what the button does.

11.title: Keep the type as Button
11.do: Check that **Button to generate counterpart entry** is selected.
actions: Check the first option is selected.
11.see: **Button to generate counterpart entry** is selected.
11.why: This type puts a button in the Reconcile screen that posts a ready-made counterpart line in one click.

12.title: Limit the button to one journal
12.why: The button then appears only when you reconcile that bank journal.
12.tip: Leave it empty to show the button on every journal.

13.title: Add the counterpart line
13.where: Model form > Counterpart Entries > Add a line
13.why: Counterpart Entries is the journal entry the button will create.

14.title: Choose the expense account
14.see: The account **72030110 BANK CHARGES** is in the line.
14.why: This is the account the charge will be posted to.

15.title: Amount Type: Percentage of balance
15.do: Leave **Amount Type** on **Percentage of balance** and **Amount** on **100**.
15.where: Counterpart Entries > Amount Type and Amount
15.why: This tells Odoo to move the whole remaining balance of the bank line to this account.

16.title: Label the journal item
16.see: The label appears in the line.
16.why: This text becomes the label on the generated journal item, which makes the entry easy to recognise later.

17.title: Save the model
actions: Look at the top left, beside the model name.
17.see: The cloud icon disappears. The model is saved.
17.why: The model is now live and its button will appear in the Reconcile screen of the Commercial Bank journal.

18.title: Go to the Accounting Dashboard
18.do: Click **Dashboard** in the top menu bar.
18.see: The bank journal cards, including **Commercial Bank**.
18.why: The model is ready. Now you will use it.

19.title: Open Reconcile on the Commercial Bank card
19.see: The reconciliation screen, with the lines still to match.
19.why: The button shows how many bank lines are still waiting to be matched.

20.title: Select the bank charge line
20.do: In the list on the left, click the **Monthly Bank Charges** line of −25.00.
20.where: Reconciliation screen > list on the left
20.see: The line opens on the right.
20.why: It is a charge the bank took, so there is no invoice to match it against.
20.tip: You can search the list to find the line quickly.

21.title: Before: the line sits in Bank Suspense
21.do: Look at the entry on the right: the other side is **12090250 BANK SUSPENSE**.
21.see: The counterpart is parked in **12090250 BANK SUSPENSE**.
21.why: Until you tell Odoo what the transaction is, the counterpart is parked in Bank Suspense. Your model will replace it.

22.title: Click the reconciliation model button
22.do: Click your model's button at the top of the entry.
actions: Look at the buttons above the entry.
22.why: One click builds the counterpart line for you, with no typing of accounts or amounts.
22.tip: Other buttons for this journal appear here too; click the right one.

23.title: After: the counterpart is ready
actions: Check the account, the amount and the label.
23.see: **Bank Suspense** has been replaced by **72030110 BANK CHARGES** for 25.00 with the label **Bank charges**.
23.why: Always read this line before validating.

24.title: Validate the reconciliation
24.see: The line disappears from the Not Matched list.
24.why: Odoo posts the journal entry and the bank line is reconciled.
24.warning: Press **Validate** only once. Odoo applies it a moment after the click.

25.title: One line less to reconcile
25.do: Look at the counter at the top: one line fewer.
actions: Look at the counter at the top right.
25.see: The counter has dropped by one and Odoo has moved on to the next unmatched line.
25.why: That is the whole button-model flow: select, click the button, validate.

26.title: Select a customer receipt line
26.do: Click a customer receipt line in the list.
26.where: Reconciliation screen > list on the left
actions: Find a customer receipt line, for example **Cheque Settlement**.
26.see: The line opens on the right, with a customer name.
26.why: This is the other kind of model: the line should be matched to an open invoice, not written off to an expense account.

27.title: Open Match Existing Entries
actions: Look at the tabs below the entry.
27.see: A list of open entries, filtered by the line's **Partner**.
27.why: Because the bank line has a partner, the matching rule narrows the list down to this customer's open items.

28.title: Pick the matching invoice
28.do: Click the customer invoice whose open amount equals the receipt.
actions: Find the invoice on the **Debtors Ledger Control** account.
28.see: The invoice appears as the counterpart above.
28.why: Clicking a candidate adds it to the reconciliation.
28.tip: If you cannot see the invoice, remove the **Partner** filter and search by invoice number.

29.title: Check the match is complete
29.do: Read the entry: the counterpart is now the invoice.
actions: Check there is no **Open balance** line.
29.see: The counterpart is the invoice and there is no **Open balance** line left.
29.why: The receipt fully settles the amount you selected.

30.title: Validate the invoice match
30.see: The receipt is posted against the invoice.
30.why: The invoice is paid down by the receipt.

31.title: Recap: which model to use when
31.do: Remember which model fits which case.
points: Use a **button model** for recurring costs with no invoice, such as bank charges, interest and small differences.
Use a **rule to match invoices/bills** for customer receipts and supplier payments.
Use a **rule to suggest a counterpart** when part of the line is a fee.
31.see: The next unmatched line, or the "all done" screen.
31.why: Choosing the right model saves the most time.
31.tip: That completes the tour: a button for bank charges, and an invoice rule for receipts.
